name: ARES Maps source manifest
data_kind: archived planetary observations, not real-time conditions
coordinate_system: IAU 2015:49900, Mars geographic, planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude

datasets.title: Jezero CTX stereo terrain model
datasets.description: Measured elevation from NASA MRO CTX stereo images, processed by USGS with Ames Stereo Pipeline. A 512 × 512 crop is bundled; slopes are calculated by ARES.
datasets.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS; USGS Astrogeology; Ames Stereo Pipeline. Laura et al. (2023), doi:10.5066/P9JKVWR3.

datasets.title: Controlled Jezero CTX / HiRISE imagery
datasets.description: NASA Mars Trek controlled orbital mosaics. CTX is shown at regional scale; HiRISE loads at close zoom. A 25-tile CTX mosaic is bundled for the starting area.
datasets.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS/University of Arizona/USGS; NASA Mars Trek.

datasets.title: Global CTX orbital mosaic
datasets.description: Global context outside the Jezero controlled mosaic. This uncontrolled mosaic can have positional offsets.

datasets.title: Viking color and MOLA relief
datasets.description: Global color imagery and color shaded relief, accessed through NASA Mars Trek. Zooming beyond source resolution enlarges pixels.
datasets.credit: NASA Viking; NASA Mars Global Surveyor / MOLA; USGS; NASA Mars Trek.

datasets.title: THEMIS day / night infrared mosaics
datasets.description: Historical Mars Odyssey infrared mosaics, 100 m, v2 October 2018. Display imagery only: no present-day or numeric surface temperatures are inferred.
datasets.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Arizona State University/USGS; NASA Mars Trek.

datasets.title: Perseverance landing coordinates
datasets.description: Landing marker: 18.44463° N, 77.45088° E. This is the 2021 landing position, not the current rover location. Other search landmarks are approximate overview points.
datasets.credit: NASA Langley Research Center, Assessment of the Mars 2020 Entry, Descent, and Landing Simulation.

datasets.title: IAU / USGS Mars named places
datasets.description: 2055 named feature centers; labels declutter by view.

datasets.title: Historic Mars landing sites
datasets.description: 12 landing missions; individual references and approximate-location flags in landings.json. Historical landing sites, not live rover positions.

datasets.title: NASA Viking globe imagery
datasets.description: 2048 x 1024 Viking MDIM21 color mosaic from NASA Mars Trek tiles; spherical globe, not detailed terrain.

datasets.title: Sol duration: NASA Mars24
datasets.description: Travel durations use 88775.244 Earth seconds per mean solar sol. Estimates exclude rest stops.

datasets.title: Perseverance Sol 3 panorama
datasets.description: NASA cylindrical 360-degree Mastcam-Z panorama at Jezero landing, February 21 2021. Viewer uses NASA-hosted preview imagery, without generated content.

datasets.title: Curiosity first-drive panorama
datasets.description: NASA 360-degree Navcam cylindrical panorama, August 22 2012. Camera marker is approximate, within the Bradbury Landing area; rover was about six metres from its landing site.

derived_products.slope: central differences on the native projected grid, east-west spacing corrected by cos(latitude); unknown neighbors remain unknown
derived_products.elevation_display: rounded to 0.1 m for storage, displayed to nearest meter; source accuracy is lower than this numerical precision
derived_products.routing: A* on eight-connected terrain cells; per-edge cost is Mars horizontal distance plus user uphill weight times positive elevation gain. Excludes missing cells, over-limit terrain and edge slopes, and diagonal corner cutting. Straight-line Mars distance is an admissible heuristic. Endpoints snap to cell centers.
derived_products.travel_time: Automatically selected transport preset: distance / speed, plus per-meter ascent allowance only for measured terrain routes. Visual estimates have unknown climbing time.
derived_products.cost_units: Equivalent flat-travel meters; adjustable planning model, not measured metabolic energy. Downhill has distance cost but no uphill surcharge.
derived_products.visual_routing: Outside measured coverage (or when selected explicitly), sample a padded endpoint window on a 128 × 128 grid from global NASA MRO CTX imagery, hosted by Esri. Local grayscale differences within a 5 × 5 cell neighborhood create a 0–1 contrast/texture proxy. Edge cost = Mars distance × (1 + user weight × mean endpoint proxy). This is an appearance-based estimate, not topographic height or slope. Missing pixels are excluded; elevation/ascent/slope remain null. Tile zoom adapts to window size. A* searches only the sampled window, not the entire planet.

challenge_resource_access_note: Challenge URL was inaccessible from this environment (certificate/HTTP errors). Original NASA Mars Trek and USGS data services were accessed directly.
source_dtm_projection: IAU 2015:49910 equirectangular, planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude
transport_preset_note: Illustrative planning assumptions selected by transport mode, not NASA-certified capability or physiological models. On foot: 2.5 km/h, 15-degree slope cap, uphill weight 10, image texture weight 10, 0.05 min per ascent meter. Rover: 6 km/h, 12-degree slope cap, uphill weight 4, image texture weight 7, 0.01 min per ascent meter. Cargo rover: 4 km/h, 10-degree slope cap, uphill weight 18, image texture weight 18, 0.03 min per ascent meter. Visual mode does not assess slopes or ascent and uses distance-based time only.
display_notes: Optional warm tint is a display filter, not measured color. Globe uses NASA color imagery. Three.js: MIT license.
